loop.label: The Fuelr loop
loop.title: Five steps that close on themselves
loop.text: Each step feeds the next: what you plan becomes your shopping list, what you cook becomes your diary, what you measure corrects the plan.

steps.title: Plan
steps.text: Drag your recipes onto the days of the week. Servings follow the household.

steps.title: Buy
steps.text: The shopping list writes itself and groups by aisle, offline in the shop.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: One step per screen, timers picked up from the text, the screen stays awake.

steps.title: Measure
steps.text: A meal you cooked is logged for you, with nothing typed twice.

steps.title: Correct
steps.text: The week's charts adjust the plan that follows.

testimonial.label: What cooks say about it
testimonial.quote: I used to spend Sundays copying recipes into a spreadsheet. Fuelr writes the shopping list on its own, and I finally know what I am eating.
testimonial.author: Salomé T. · 4 people, 2 batch cooks a week

features.label: Features
features.title: Everything you need, nothing decorative
features.text: Nine product journeys, one rule: every screen has an obvious action. Here is what you will actually use each week.

items.title: Recipe editor
items.text: Title, photo, servings, ingredients, steps you can reorder. The draft exists from the first click — no “do you want to save?” dialog.

items.title: Import from a link
items.text: Paste a recipe's URL: ingredients and steps are pulled out, and anything guessed is marked “needs a look”.

items.title: The week's plan
items.text: Seven days, four meals, drag and drop. Servings follow how many people are eating.

items.title: Nutrition as you go
items.text: Kcal and macros per serving recomputed on every change. Never on request, never approximate without saying so.

items.title: Shopping list
items.text: Written from the plan, grouped by aisle, ticked one-handed, working with no network.

items.title: Estimate a plate from a photo
items.text: One photo, one editable estimate in under 20 seconds. Estimated and measured stay visibly apart.

cooking.title: Cooking mode
cooking.text: One step per screen, larger text, the screen kept awake, timers read from the text. Dirty hands never need a precise gesture.
points: 56px targets, maximum contrast, no precise gesture anywhere.
Timers read from the step's own words (“15 min”) and rung in the background.
Interrupted without loss: “Curry — step 3 of 5” waiting when you come back.

pricing.label: Pricing
pricing.title: One price, not a maze
pricing.text: The free plan is genuinely usable: unlimited recipes and the full weekly plan. You pay for the deeper nutrition and for sharing with a household.

plans.name: Fuelr Plus
plans.pitch: Nutrition in full: macros, targets, history and charts.

items.question: Is the free plan limited in time?
items.answer: No. Recipes, the plan and the shopping list stay free with no time limit and no cap. Nothing is cut off after 14 days.

items.question: Do my recipes belong to me?
items.answer: Yes, and you can export all of them as a readable file at any moment — including after cancelling.

items.question: Does it work without a network?
items.answer: Cooking mode, the shopping list and photos work offline. Everything syncs when the network comes back.

items.question: How are the nutrition figures worked out?
items.answer: From a reference food table. An ingredient it could not recognise is marked “estimated” — a guessed value is never presented as a measured one.

launch.title: Everything is open during the launch
launch.body: The plans below describe what will become paid. Today, Fuelr Plus and Family are open to everybody, with no card. We will say so before that changes, and nothing already written will be deleted.

about.label: About
about.title: We just wanted to know what to eat on Tuesday
about.text: Fuelr came out of a spreadsheet shared between four flatmates who cooked a lot and measured badly. We kept the spreadsheet's rigour and threw away its ugliness: honest figures, recipes that can be planned, and nothing that makes you feel bad.

principles.title: Estimated is not measured
principles.text: A guessed value is flagged everywhere it appears. We would rather say “we don't know” than give you a wrong number.

principles.title: One screen, one action
principles.text: A single primary button per view. The alternatives are secondary or written in text, never shouting.

principles.title: Nothing that shames you
principles.text: No streak to keep, no guilt-trip notification. The data is there to help you decide, not to punish you.

team.title: The team
team.text: Four people, one office, a great deal of washing up.

privacy.label: Data
privacy.title: Where your data goes
privacy.text: Fuelr is a cooking app, not an advertising business. This page says what is kept, what leaves the application, and where it goes.

sections.title: What Fuelr keeps
sections.text: Your account — email address, first name, a one-way encrypted password — and what you write in the application: recipes and photos, the week's plan, the shopping list, the meal diary, your household and its invitations. Nothing else is collected: no advertising trackers, no analytics, no profile sold on.

sections.title: The AI features are processed abroad
sections.text: The AI features — reading a badly marked-up recipe page, estimating a photographed plate, transcribing a page from a book — rely on Anthropic, in the United States. What you hand to those features, the photo or the page's content, therefore leaves Switzerland for the length of the analysis. They are optional and part of a paid plan: as long as you do not use them, nothing is sent to Anthropic.

sections.title: The two other ways out
items: Emails — address confirmation, password reset — go through a sending service based outside Switzerland, which sees your address and the message.
When you import a recipe from a link, it is Fuelr that fetches the page and its photo. The site you are importing from sees a request from our servers, never from your browser.

sections.title: What stays on your device
sections.text: Cooking mode and the offline shopping list keep a copy on the machine you are using, so that a kitchen with no network is not a dead end; that copy is wiped when you sign out. One cookie is set, the one that keeps you signed in, and there is none for analytics or advertising.

sections.title: Your recipes stay yours
sections.text: Exporting all of your recipes is available from the library, at any time and with no conditions — including after cancelling, which deletes nothing. To have your account and its contents erased, write to us: it is handled by hand today, and it is handled.
